properties.name: mass_response
properties.description:

return a typed Mass envelope place the same JSON graph here that
the typed envelope would expose under `mass_response`.

When a producer also emits `output_facts`, `mass_response` MUST be
field-for-field identical to `output_facts`. Like `output_facts`,
this slot is transport-facing and excluded from
`canonical_signing_bytes`; the load-bearing binding remains
`claim_digest` over the audit payload.

properties.name: non_admissible_reasons

properties.name: output_facts
properties.description:
Pragmatic immediate-consumer-facing facts surfaced alongside the
envelope. The Lever 3 supremum cutover (2026-05-01) absorbed the
previous typed-CRUD response shape (e.g. `{ key, preview_url }` for
dynamic-letters generators, `{ headers, data }` for CSV exports)
into the audit_payload behind `claim_digest`. Some immediate
consumers (the Mass webapp dynamic-letter and statement consumers)
still need to read those exact fields without having to walk the
audit-event stream. `output_facts` carries the same JSON body that
rode the typed response, so the wire signature for those consumers
reduces to `proof.output_facts?.<field>`.

`output_facts` is NOT part of the canonical signing body: it lives
outside `canonical_signing_bytes` and does NOT contribute to
`claim_digest` or `bundle_digest`. The signed binding for the same
information is `claim_digest` over the audit_payload; `output_facts`
is a transport-side convenience that mirrors the audit_payload
fields the webapp displays. Producers that emit `output_facts` MUST
keep it byte-equivalent to the corresponding subset of the
audit_payload that produced `claim_digest`; consumers that need
load-bearing assurance MUST verify `claim_digest` against the
audit_payload, never against `output_facts`.

`None` is the only "no facts" state at the wire boundary.
Producers populate `Some(value)` for surfaced facts; absence is
represented by `None`, which omits the key from the serialized
envelope (`#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`).
`Some(Value::Null)` is functionally aliased to `None` because
serde's default `Option<serde_json::Value>` deserializer collapses
JSON `null` to `None`; producers MUST NOT rely on a
`Some(Value::Null)` "surfaced but empty" distinction. Callers that
need to communicate "we generated a proof but produced no facts"
should leave `output_facts` as `None` and rely on the absence of
the JSON key as the wire signal.
